title: Postgres connection exhaustion
steps: Check active connections: SELECT usename, state, count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY 1, 2;
Identify idle-in-transaction sessions older than 5 minutes and terminate them.
Confirm app pool_size and max_overflow match Postgres max_connections.
Restart the leaking worker only after the pool config is corrected.
Watch p99 latency and connection count for 15 minutes before closing.

title: Redis cache stampede
steps: Enable request coalescing / singleflight on the hottest cache keys.
Stop any cache-flush jobs. Warm the top keys before reopening traffic.
Stagger TTLs so keys do not expire together.
If Redis is saturated, fail closed to stale cache rather than the origin DB.
Confirm origin QPS returned to baseline before ending the incident.

title: Pod CrashLoopBackOff / OOMKill
steps: kubectl describe pod and confirm Last State is OOMKilled or Error.
Compare memory limit to recent working-set from metrics.
Roll back the last config or image that increased batch size or concurrency.
Quarantine poison messages if a queue consumer is involved.
Raise limits only after the leak or batch-size issue is fixed.
